description:
Nuestra Visión:
Queremos construir una herramienta visual e interactiva que no solo muestre un mapa de Marte, sino que cuente una historia. Integraremos datos reales de los rovers de la NASA para trazar rutas seguras, identificar peligros y encontrar recursos en el terreno marciano.
summary: MARS GUARDIAN is an interactive web platform that integrates planetary mapping, preliminary risk assessment and topographic route planning to support the first astronauts on Mars. It combines a Three.js 3D globe with a Leaflet 2D map built on NASA/JPL Mars Trek, organized into 13 regions, 52 sectors and 33 locations of interest in the Ladon Basin, with layers for points of interest, hazard zones and routes. From NASA PDS MOLA MEGDR data we built one global and three regional cost maps that weight seven risk factors. An A* search on an 8-neighbor grid finds the lowest-cost route, and each area is classified as low, caution, high or insufficient data. The prototype includes a web dashboard, an astronaut app with live telemetry, and passes 27 of 27 automated tests. It is complemented by the Astralin rover, with a passive rocker-bogie suspension, a bevel-gear differential, 100 kg payload capacity and a 5-DOF robotic arm. This addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge: a Martian walk can be planned using real terrain data, not distance alone.
details:
MARS GUARDIAN is an interactive web platform for planning a Martian walk.

  • A Three.js 3D globe lets the user navigate Mars and select locations.
  • A Leaflet 2D map built on NASA/JPL Mars Trek shows layers for points of interest, hazard zones and routes.
  • Locations are organized into 13 regions, 52 sectors and 33 sites in the Ladon Basin.
  • From NASA PDS MOLA MEGDR elevation data we generated one global and three regional cost maps that weight seven terrain risk factors.
  • Haversine computes distances, and an A* search on an 8-neighbor grid finds the lowest-cost route.
  • Each area is classified as low risk, caution, high risk or insufficient data. Missing data is never treated as safe.
  • A companion astronaut app receives live telemetry through WebSocket and Firebase.

Benefits and expected impact

  • Astronauts and mission planners get one layered view instead of scattered data, so they can compare routes by real terrain difficulty and not just by distance.
  • The method is transferable to the Moon and to remote areas on Earth.
  • Next steps are higher-resolution HiRISE topography, real rover telemetry and a physical prototype.

Tools and technologies

  • Software: JavaScript, React and Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Three.js, Node.js, WebSocket and Firebase.
  • Testing: 27 automated Node.js tests, all passing, covering routing, cost maps, the server and the Firebase bridge.
  • Data: NASA/JPL Mars Trek, NASA PDS MOLA MEGDR and USGS geologic mapping of Ladon Basin.
  • Rover engineering: SolidWorks for CAD, MATLAB for kinematics and structural calculations, and Three.js with glTF for 3D visualization and animation.

Creativity

  • The project joins geospatial analysis and mechanical engineering in a single mission concept.
  • The Astralin rover is designed to carry the route the platform plans. It has a passive rocker-bogie suspension with a bevel-gear differential that keeps all six wheels on the ground, 100 kg of payload, 30° slope capability, a 5-DOF robotic arm and a pan/tilt sensor mast that collects terrain data along the traverse.
  • The rover’s structure was verified for Mars gravity (3.71 m/s²) against NASA-STD-5001 safety factors.

Factors the team considered

  • Astronaut safety and the honest handling of uncertainty: an A* route is not automatically a safe route, and the global map is kilometer-scale (~42 km per cell).
  • Use of only real, citable NASA data.
  • Clarity of the interface under mission pressure.
  • Materials, mass and energy limits for the rover: 6061-T6 aluminum and AISI 4340 steel, and about 2.6 kWh per traverse.
  • Scalability toward higher-resolution data.
